findings.scope: For arbitrary G and normal N: B7(N)<=2, B7(G/N)<=2 and quotient 3-Helly imply B7(G)<=5; without Helly any bad six-family has a non-Helly quotient-overlap triangle. General threshold/Ramsey version and exact actual-fiber identity included.

For arbitrary G and normal N: B_T(N)<=r plus index-only J_T(G/N)<=s imply B_T(G)<=r+s, with repeated subgroup labels, arbitrary finite-index LEFT cosets, and no quotient Helly, split or finite G hypothesis. In particular B7(N)<=5 plus J7(Q)<=2 imply Sun8(G). Elementary all-p>7 matrix proof gives J7(PSL2(p))<=2 and a quotient triple showing J7<=2 does not imply 3-Helly; that triple's index p+1 exceeds seven and is not a bad-gcd example. Parent-supported A8 kernel and an infinite rational kernel are exact scoped applications.

remaining_original_gap: The original unrestricted arbitrary-group Sun8 assertion remains open. The sparse quotient hypothesis fails for every finite s when Q has a proper subgroup of index at most seven, and arbitrary N need not satisfy B7<=5. The first bridge requires a stronger-than-Sun8 packing bound and quotient 3-Helly. Neither theorem removes these premises, promotes the unfrozen simple-group assembly or adopts f184/f188/A7/Fano candidates.
